## §W9-1. S93-W9-1-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR

```yaml
# ---- Identity (4 fields) ----
gate_id: "S93-W9-1-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[AUDIT]"   # plan-freeze audit-script authorship; PASS = the validator catches all known drift instances (artifact-existence + calibration-corpus coverage)
classification: "NON-PHONONIC"   # methodology / audit-floor tooling (the F-image of the substrate PRU-drift problem at the audit layer)
agent_type: "gen-physicist"
hypothesis: "A plan-freeze validator that greps each plan-block input_files `section_anchor_lines: \"L1-L2\"` field (and bare registry line citations) against the CURRENT registry heading-line index — via heading-anchor grep, not line-number trust — catches all four S92 drift instances (§VII.AR +106, §VII.AW.OP-PROJ +229, §VII.U.2 +56-equivalent, S92 W5 ~150-line) at plan-freeze BEFORE dispatch, emitting S2 advisory at drift>50 lines and S1 MANDATORY at drift>200 lines, and integrates as an extension of `_plan_upstream_pin_validator.py`."

method:
  description: >
    Author a plan-freeze validator (extending `computations/_shared/_plan_upstream_pin_validator.py`) that
    for every session plan-file (`sessions/session-plan/session-{N}-plan-w*.md`):
      (1) regex-extracts every `section_anchor_lines: "L1-L2"` field AND every bare registry line citation
          of the form `lines NNNN-MMMM` / `line ~NNNN` / `at registry lines NNNN` adjacent to a
          `permanent-results-registry.md` mention in a plan-block;
      (2) for each citation, extracts the ASSOCIATED registry HEADING anchor (the `### §VII.X ...` or
          `## §VII.X ...` heading the citation claims to point at — parsed from the surrounding plan text /
          gate_id / hypothesis);
      (3) greps the CURRENT `sessions/permanent-results-registry.md` for that heading anchor, returning its
          actual line number L_actual;
      (4) computes drift = |L_plan_center − L_actual| where L_plan_center = (L1+L2)/2 for a range or the bare
          line for a point citation;
      (5) emits severity per the pre-registered band: drift ≤ 50 → NO-ACTION; 50 < drift ≤ 200 → S2 ADVISORY;
          drift > 200 → S1 MANDATORY (halts plan-freeze with runtime-rescue recommendation per
          `substrate-first-canonical-sourcing.md §(ii.B)`).
    The validator runs a SELF-TEST against the S92 W4/W5 calibration corpus: a fixture plan-block citing the
    PRE-DRIFT line numbers (§VII.AR plan-pinned 17170-17208; §VII.AW.OP-PROJ plan-pinned 18020/18054) against
    a fixture registry with the POST-DRIFT headings (§VII.AR at 17276-17326; §VII.AW.OP-PROJ at 18213-18289)
    MUST fire the correct severity (the §VII.AW +229 case fires S1 MANDATORY; the §VII.AR +106 and §VII.U.2
    +56 cases fire S2 ADVISORY; the S92 W5 ~150-line case fires S2 ADVISORY). PASS = all four corpus
    instances detected at the correct severity AND no false-positive on a zero-drift fixture.
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/_plan_line_anchor_validator.py"   # NEW audit script; integrates with _plan_upstream_pin_validator.py

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----

# (1) operator
operator:
  type: "set"   # METHODOLOGY/audit-class: a calibration-corpus coverage test (4 instances at correct severity) + 1 no-false-positive test
  form: >
    PASS iff ALL of: (a) §VII.AR +106 drift detected at S2 ADVISORY (50 < 106 ≤ 200);
                     AND (b) §VII.AW.OP-PROJ +229 drift detected at S1 MANDATORY (229 > 200);
                     AND (c) §VII.U.2 +56 drift detected at S2 ADVISORY (50 < 56 ≤ 200);
                     AND (d) S92 W5 ~150-line drift detected at S2 ADVISORY (50 < ~150 ≤ 200);
                     AND (e) zero-drift fixture returns NO-ACTION (no false-positive).
    The severity bands are the PRE-REGISTERED thresholds: drift_S2_floor=50, drift_S1_floor=200.

# (2) strict_PASS_boundary
strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "5-of-5 calibration tests pass (4 true-positive at correct severity band + 1 true-negative); artifact-existence-with-content: _plan_line_anchor_validator.py present + self-test __main__ block + integration hook into _plan_upstream_pin_validator.py"
  direction: "="   # boolean conjunction over the 5 calibration tests

# (3) boundary_reachable_analytically
boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: "The drift values are EXACT integers from the S92 W4 process observation (`session-92-w4-workingpaper.md:762`: §VII.AR +106 = 17276−17170; §VII.AW.OP-PROJ +229 = 18249−18020 midpoint; §VII.U.2 +56-equivalent) + the S92 W5 ~150-line drift. The severity bands (50/200) are the pre-registered thresholds from CF-S93-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR (`session-92-w4-workingpaper.md:799`). Detection is a deterministic grep + integer subtraction; no numerical iteration."

# (4) reachable_rationals
reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: true
  mesh_density: "discrete — drift is an integer line-count difference; severity bands are integer thresholds (50, 200)"

# (5) machinery_pin_map — every free parameter of producing_script, pinned
machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "5"                         # 4 true-positive calibration tests + 1 true-negative
  L_max: "N/A — audit-script (no spectral computation)"
  scan_range: "N/A — deterministic grep over plan-files + registry"
  step_size: "N/A"
  tolerance: "0 — integer line-count comparison; drift is exact"
  scheme: "PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-DRIFT-HEADING-GREP-VALIDATOR"
  convention: "section_anchor_lines-vs-current-registry-heading-grep-S2-at-drift-gt-50-S1-at-drift-gt-200"
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "cpu-cap-OMP8"           # text grep + integer arithmetic; no linear algebra
  drift_S2_floor: "50"               # S2 ADVISORY threshold (lines)
  drift_S1_floor: "200"              # S1 MANDATORY threshold (lines)
  calibration_corpus: "[(VII.AR,+106,S2),(VII.AW.OP-PROJ,+229,S1),(VII.U.2,+56,S2),(S92-W5,~150,S2)]"   # 4 true-positive instances
  integration_target: "computations/_shared/_plan_upstream_pin_validator.py"   # the existing validator this extends

# (6) audit_discriminators
audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap"]   # canonical = the calibration-corpus drift values + severity bands
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

# (7) substitution_chain — required (the gate makes a directional severity claim: drift>200 ⇒ S1; drift>50 ⇒ S2)
substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "drift > 200 lines fires S1 MANDATORY (strictly more severe than the S2 ADVISORY band 50 < drift ≤ 200)."

    Step 1: drift := |L_plan_center − L_actual|   [definition; L_plan_center from section_anchor_lines midpoint, L_actual from current-registry heading grep]
    Step 2: severity(drift) := NO-ACTION if drift ≤ 50; S2 if 50 < drift ≤ 200; S1 if drift > 200   [pre-registered band map from CF-S93-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR]
    Step 3: Substitute the §VII.AW.OP-PROJ instance: drift = 229   [from session-92-w4-workingpaper.md:762 process observation]
    Step 4: Simplify: 229 > 200 ⇒ severity(229) = S1 MANDATORY   [band map evaluation]
            Substitute the §VII.AR instance: drift = 106; 50 < 106 ≤ 200 ⇒ severity(106) = S2 ADVISORY
            Substitute the §VII.U.2 instance: drift = 56; 50 < 56 ≤ 200 ⇒ severity(56) = S2 ADVISORY
            Substitute the S92 W5 instance: drift ≈ 150; 50 < 150 ≤ 200 ⇒ severity(150) = S2 ADVISORY
    Step 5: Direction: the severity map is MONOTONE NON-DECREASING in drift (larger drift ⇒ at-least-as-severe);
            the §VII.AW +229 case is the SOLE S1 in the corpus precisely because it is the only drift > 200.
    Conclusion: the validator's severity-band map is monotone in drift; the four corpus instances partition as
    {S1: §VII.AW +229} ∪ {S2: §VII.AR +106, §VII.U.2 +56, S92-W5 ~150}; PASS requires the validator reproduce
    this exact partition AND return NO-ACTION on the zero-drift true-negative.

# (8) input_files — every file producing_script reads, with SHA pin
input_files:
  plan_upstream_pin_validator:
    path: "computations/_shared/_plan_upstream_pin_validator.py"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"   # the existing validator the new audit extends/integrates with
  permanent_results_registry:
    path: "sessions/permanent-results-registry.md"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"   # the live audit target (current heading-line index)
  s92_w4_workingpaper:
    path: "sessions/archive/session-92/session-92-w4-workingpaper.md"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"   # calibration-corpus source: the 3 W4 drift instances (line 762) + CF spec (799-802)

# ---- Output artifacts ----
output_artifacts:
  script:
    path: "computations/_shared/_plan_line_anchor_validator.py"
    artifact_kind: "script"
    must_contain:
      - "section_anchor_lines"
      - "drift_S1_floor"
      - "__main__"            # self-test driver against the calibration corpus
  data:
    path: "computations/session-93/s93_w9_1_plan_line_anchor_validator_selftest.json"
    artifact_kind: "data"
    optional: false           # JSON sidecar: the 5 calibration-test results (4 true-positive severities + 1 true-negative)
  plot:
    path: "computations/session-93/s93_w9_1_plan_line_anchor_validator.png"
    artifact_kind: "plot"
    optional: true            # audit-script gate; no physics plot (a drift-vs-severity bar chart is OPTIONAL)
  verdict_line:
    path: "computations/session-93/s93_gate_verdicts.txt"
    artifact_kind: "verdict_line"
    must_contain: "^S93-W9-1-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR:.* audit_sha256=[a-f0-9]{64}"
    companion_row_required: true
    schema_v2_3tuple_required: false
  wp_section:
    path: "sessions/archive/session-93/session-93-w9-workingpaper.md"
    artifact_kind: "wp_section"
    section_anchor: "### §W9-1. S93-W9-1-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR"
    must_contain:
      - "\\*\\*Status\\*\\*:.*COMPLETED"
      - "\\*\\*Verdict\\*\\*:.*(PASS|FAIL|INFO)"
      - "\\*\\*Output Artifacts\\*\\*"
      - "\\*\\*MCP Pre-Compute Audit\\*\\*"

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  The plan-line-anchor validator exists, self-tests against the S92 W4/W5 calibration corpus, and detects all
  four known drift instances at their correct severity band (§VII.AW.OP-PROJ +229 → S1; §VII.AR +106, §VII.U.2
  +56, S92 W5 ~150 → S2) with no false-positive on the zero-drift fixture. The S92 W4/W5 plan-text-drift failure
  mode — where agents had to runtime-rescue stale registry line citations per `substrate-first-canonical-sourcing.md
  §(ii.B)` — is now caught at PLAN-FREEZE, BEFORE dispatch. This is the audit-floor F-image of the substrate PRU
  prevention: a drift caught at plan-freeze never reaches an agent's runtime.
FAIL_meaning: >
  The validator misses any of the four known drift instances, OR mis-classifies a severity (e.g., the +229 case
  fires only S2 instead of S1), OR fires a false-positive on the zero-drift fixture. A FAIL means the validator
  cannot be trusted to catch live S93 drift (which the W5 planner just hit), so the S2/S1 routing remains a
  runtime-rescue burden on agents rather than a plan-freeze gate. Per `math-scripts.md §"Exit Codes"`, a FAIL
  verdict is a valid result (the validator's coverage is incomplete), not a script crash; remediation extends
  the regex / severity-band logic.
INFO_meaning: >
  The validator detects all four drift instances but one severity-band boundary is ambiguous at runtime (e.g.,
  the §VII.U.2 "+56-equivalent" is a grep-anchor-validated drift rather than a direct line-difference, so its
  drift integer is heuristic) — INFO records the 3 unambiguous detections + the integration hook while flagging
  the heuristic instance for a tighter regex in a follow-up.

# ---- Effort + framing ----
effort:
  files_created:
    - "computations/_shared/_plan_line_anchor_validator.py"
    - "computations/session-93/s93_w9_1_plan_line_anchor_validator_selftest.json"
  estimated_time: "~0.5 wave-equivalent (extend existing audit machinery + self-test against the W4/W5 calibration corpus)"

substrate_framing: |
  NON-PHONONIC (methodology / audit-floor tooling). This gate carries no substrate-physics computation; it is the
  audit-floor F-image (per `epistemic-discipline.md §"Layer-Decomposition"`) of the substrate PRU-drift problem.
  Under the layer-functor F: substrate → methodology → audit, a plan-pinned registry line number is the methodology-
  floor image of a substrate machinery-pin (the upstream gate's output the plan-block consumes), and the line-anchor
  validator is the audit-line image of the substrate's numerical PASS-predicate. The validator does NOT compute any
  D_K eigenvalue; it enforces that the methodology-floor citations (plan-block section_anchor_lines) remain coherent
  with the registry's actual structure — the audit-floor discipline that keeps the substrate-physics gates'
  provenance traceable. Container-thinking is N/A (no substrate observable); the methodology contribution is the
  plan-freeze drift-catch that prevents the S92 W4/W5 runtime-rescue burden from recurring in S93.

# ---- METHODOLOGY-class M1-M4 self-classification (wave-classification.md) ----
# M1 (PASS-predicate = artifact-existence-with-content): SATISFIED — calibration-corpus coverage (5 boolean tests) + validator-exists-with-self-test; no substrate numerical threshold (the drift integers are audit-layer line counts, not physics observables).
# M2 (producing-op = Edit/Write on .py audit script + grep/integer-count): SATISFIED — audit-script authorship + grep over plan-files/registry + integer subtraction; no eigenvalue/linalg/FFT, no fixture-with-hand-engineered-physics-target.
# M3 (source-of-truth = verbatim from closed S92 W4 process observation): SATISFIED — the 4 drift instances + severity bands are verbatim from `session-92-w4-workingpaper.md:762,799-802` (closed-S92); no new derivation.
# M4 (allowlist membership): REQUIRES ORCHESTRATOR APPEND — gate-ID "S93-W9-1-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR" must be appended to
#     sessions/framework/registry/methodology-wave-allowlist-ledger.md at plan-freeze (orchestrator-only edit per recursion-attack closure,
#     `methodology-wave-allowlist.md §"Edit discipline"`); until appended, M4 FAILS and the gate falls through to COMPUTE-class.
#     ***FLAG FOR ORCHESTRATOR ALLOWLIST APPEND*** (3-column ledger row | S93-W9-1-PLAN-LINE-ANCHOR-VALIDATOR | S93 | <sha256_of_plan_block> | + parallel rationale entry in methodology-wave-instances.md).
```

## §W9-2. S93-W9-2-PLAN-CORPUS-SECTION-NUMBER-DRIFT-DETECTOR

```yaml
# ---- Identity (4 fields) ----
gate_id: "S93-W9-2-PLAN-CORPUS-SECTION-NUMBER-DRIFT-DETECTOR"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[AUDIT]"   # audit-script extension; PASS = grep-cross-check catches the §15-vs-§17 W6-2 calibration instance at plan-freeze
classification: "NON-PHONONIC"   # methodology / audit-floor tooling (plan-vs-corpus section-number coherence)
agent_type: "gen-physicist"
hypothesis: "An audit-script extension to `_source_reconciliation_audit.py` that grep-cross-checks every plan-file corpus-section-number reference (e.g. plan §W6-2's `cross-pillar-bridge-corpus.md §15`) against the corpus-file's actual table-of-contents (§1-§24) catches the S92 W6-2 §15-vs-§17 drift at plan-freeze — where plan §W6-2 referenced corpus '§15 Within-cell discriminator axes' but the actual authority is §17 (§15 = Level-3 anchor singleness)."

method:
  description: >
    Extend `computations/_shared/_source_reconciliation_audit.py` with a new sub-detector
    `detect_plan_corpus_section_number_drift(plan_text, corpus_path)` that:
      (1) parses the corpus-file's table-of-contents — every `## §N. <title>` heading in
          `sessions/framework/registry/cross-pillar-bridge-corpus.md` → a {section_number: title} map;
      (2) regex-extracts every plan-file reference of the form `cross-pillar-bridge-corpus.md §N` (or
          `corpus §N`, or `corpus.md §N`) PLUS the adjacent descriptive phrase the plan uses to NAME that
          section (e.g. "§15 Within-cell discriminator axes");
      (3) for each reference, compares the plan's descriptive phrase against the corpus TOC title at that
          section number; if the plan's phrase MATCHES a DIFFERENT section's title than the cited number,
          emit `PLAN-CORPUS-SECTION-NUMBER-DRIFT` naming both the cited-§N and the correct-§M;
      (4) self-tests against the S92 W6-2 instance: plan reference "§15 Within-cell discriminator axes" vs
          corpus TOC (§15 = "Level-3 anchor singleness sub-clause"; §17 = "Within-cell discriminator axes
          (α/β/γ/δ)") MUST fire DRIFT with cited=§15, correct=§17.
    Severity: S2 ADVISORY (documentation drift; the runtime canonical-path rescue per §(ii.B) handled it

  methodology contribution is preventing the recurrence of CF-S93-W6-7's plan-vs-corpus section-number mismatch.
```

```yaml
        CLOSED), with the closure rationale (Richardson sub-geometric divergence + σ_β persistence under FB
        saturation) recorded in the open-channels ledger + the corpus.
    The verdict is emitted as a workshop closure record (NOT a numerical PASS/FAIL); the corresponding registry/
    corpus/open-channel edit is a SEPARATE follow-up landing (mack sole-writer for any corpus row).

method:
  description: >
    Dispatch a 2-agent / 3-round adversarial workshop via /rclab-workshop on the shared document
    `sessions/archive/session-93/workshops/s93-w9-5-layer-functor-f-reformulation.md`. R1: each agent steelmans their
    reading (lizzi: REFORMULATE-to-K=2-weak survives; landau: CLOSE). R2: each responds to the opponent's best
    case. R3: converge on the STRUCTURAL VERDICT (A reformulate vs B close). The workshop reads the S91 W5
    predecessor adjudication + S92 W8-1 Reading_Hybrid convergence + the §W9-5 Richardson divergence data + the
    §W9-3 CF-W6-4-S91-1 σ_β=1.065 result as inputs. NO numerical compute (the σ_β and α_sub values are already on
    disk from S91/S92); the workshop ADJUDICATES their structural meaning. The closure record is the deliverable.
  producing_script: "N/A — workshop dispatch (no producing script; the deliverable is the workshop closure document + a verdict-line record of the STRUCTURAL VERDICT)"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) — workshop-adapted ----

# (1) operator
operator:
  type: "set"   # the workshop's output is a categorical STRUCTURAL VERDICT ∈ {REFORMULATE-K2-weak, CLOSE}, not a numerical comparison
  form: >
    The workshop converges (R3) on exactly ONE of: VERDICT-A (REFORMULATE-to-K=2-weak) or VERDICT-B (CLOSE).
    PASS (workshop-complete) iff: R1/R2/R3 all present in the shared doc AND a single STRUCTURAL VERDICT is
    pinned in R3 AND the verdict's evidence basis (§W9-5 Richardson α_sub=0.876 + §W9-3 σ_β=1.065) is cited.

# (2) strict_PASS_boundary
strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "workshop-complete: 3 rounds present + single STRUCTURAL VERDICT pinned in R3 + evidence basis cited; the verdict (A or B) is the OUTPUT, not a threshold"
  direction: "="   # categorical (workshop converges on one verdict)

# (3) boundary_reachable_analytically
boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: false   # adversarial adjudication — the verdict is reached by structural argument, not analytic derivation
  proof_ref: "null — the workshop's verdict is an adjudication of competing structural readings (per Investigating-Workshops.md §'Definition: A WORKSHOP IS'), not an analytically-reachable boundary. The INPUTS (α_sub=0.876, σ_β=1.065) are analytically fixed (S91/S92 outputs); the VERDICT (reformulate vs close) is the structural adjudication."

# (4) reachable_rationals
reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false   # categorical verdict; no numerical mesh
  mesh_density: "N/A — adversarial workshop; the output is a categorical STRUCTURAL VERDICT, not a numerical value"

# (5) machinery_pin_map — workshop-adapted (the 'machinery' is the participant selection + round structure)
machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "2"                    # 2 agents
  L_max: "N/A — no compute (inputs are on disk from S91/S92)"
  scan_range: "N/A"
  step_size: "N/A"
  tolerance: "N/A — categorical verdict"
  scheme: "ADVERSARIAL-WORKSHOP-2-AGENT-3-ROUND-LAYER-FUNCTOR-F-REFORMULATION"
  convention: "R1-steelman-R2-respond-R3-converge-STRUCTURAL-VERDICT-reformulate-K2-weak-vs-close"
  random_seed: "N/A — adversarial adjudication"
  GPU_path: "N/A — no compute"
  rounds: "3"
  axis_A_agent: "lizzi-spectral-functional-theorist"
  axis_B_agent: "landau-condensed-matter-theorist"
  excluded_agents: "[volovik (S92 W8-1 Axis-B co-author), connes (S91 W5 two-layer-theorem author)]"   # downstream-inheritance reach exclusion
  evidence_basis: "[§W9-5 Richardson α_sub=0.876 anchor-crossing-L=10, §W9-3 CF-W6-4-S91-1 σ_β=1.065 persists-under-FB-saturation]"

# (6) audit_discriminators
audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap"]   # canonical = the S91 W5 + S92 W8-1 predecessor convergence + the §W9-5/§W9-3 evidence; script = the workshop doc
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

# (7) substitution_chain
substitution_chain:
  required: false   # adversarial workshop; the verdict is a structural adjudication, not a sign/direction/threshold compute claim. The evidence (α_sub, σ_β) is analytically fixed; the workshop adjudicates its meaning.
  content: |
    N/A — adversarial reformulation workshop. The σ_β=1.065 and α_sub=0.876 values are OUTPUTS of S91/S92 gates
    (analytically fixed, on disk); the workshop's job is to adjudicate whether they REFORMULATE or CLOSE the K=2
    SUGGESTION, not to re-derive them. No new sign/direction/threshold claim ⇒ no substitution chain. (The
    DIRECTIONAL reading — α_sub=0.876 < 1 means SUB-geometric divergence i.e. NON-convergence to the universal
    exponent — is the workshop's adjudication content, argued by the participants, not a pre-registered compute.)

# (8) input_files — workshop inputs
input_files:

      - "\\*\\*Verdict\\*\\*:.*(REFORMULATE|CLOSE|PASS|INFO)"
      - "\\*\\*Output Artifacts\\*\\*"
      - "\\*\\*MCP Pre-Compute Audit\\*\\*"

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  The workshop converges on a single STRUCTURAL VERDICT. VERDICT-A (REFORMULATE-to-K=2-weak): the Layer-Functor F
  theorem survives as a per-FI-sub-projection-per-observable envelope statement; the BROADER sub-projection-LEVEL
  universal reading is retired and the §W9-5 Richardson + §W9-3 σ_β=1.065 evidence is folded in as its falsification;
  the K=2 SUGGESTION is retained at the narrower layer. VERDICT-B (CLOSE): the universal-envelope reading is
  untenable at every layer; FALSIFIED-at-K=2 is promoted to CLOSED with the Richardson + σ_β closure rationale. In
  EITHER case the workshop produced a NEW pinned position (the definition of a genuine Q1 workshop per
  Investigating-Workshops.md). The follow-up registry/corpus/open-channel edit is a separate mack-sole-writer landing.
FAIL_meaning: >
  The workshop does NOT converge (R3 has two competing verdicts with no resolution) OR a participant-selection
  violation surfaces (an excluded agent — volovik/connes — was dispatched, breaking the without-prior-workshop-
  context protocol per joint-theorem-promotion.md §"Stage-2 Axis-B Selection Protocol"). A FAIL routes to a
  re-dispatch with corrected participants or a third-round extension; the K=2 status is unchanged pending convergence.
INFO_meaning: >
  The workshop converges but on a THIRD reading not pre-registered (e.g., "reformulate AND defer the FB-saturation
  question to a compute gate" — a hybrid of A and B). INFO records the converged hybrid position + flags the
  deferred compute as a S94+ carry-forward; the K=2 status is updated per the hybrid verdict's narrower claim.

# ---- Effort + framing ----
effort:
  files_created:
    - "sessions/archive/session-93/workshops/s93-w9-5-layer-functor-f-reformulation.md"
    - "computations/session-93/s93_w9_5_layer_functor_f_reformulation_verdict.json"
  estimated_time: "~1.0 wave-equivalent (2-agent / 3-round adversarial workshop; inputs on disk, no new compute)"

substrate_framing: |
  GEOMETRIC. The dispute IS about the substrate-IS universal-envelope scope of the Layer-Functor F theorem at the
  F_2-axis FI-sub-projection layer. The substrate IS the finite spectral triple (A_K, H_K, D_K) at τ_fold=0.190;
  the universal-envelope clause IS a substrate-IS statement about the convergence rate of the substrate's finite-L
  Mellin-cone closure (at substrate-distance-1 pole s=3) to its L→∞ asymptotic image. The Richardson sub-geometric
  divergence (α_sub=0.876 < 1, anchor-crossing L=10) is the substrate's signature that the per-FI-sub-projection
  envelope does NOT converge to a single universal exponent; the σ_β=1.065 persistence under Friedrich-Bär
  saturation is the substrate's signature that channel-specific envelopes scatter even at the saturation limit.
  Direction of explanation: D_K eigenvalues → finite-L Mellin-cone closure → per-(projector,bridge,pole) subleading
  structure → empirical α exponent / cross-observable σ_β → the universal-vs-per-channel adjudication. Treating the
  L^{-α} envelope as a universal property of a meta-geometric container is a container-thinking violation (FORBIDDEN);
  the workshop adjudicates the substrate-IS convergence structure, not a property imposed on the substrate.

# ---- This is a WORKSHOP dispatch, NOT a METHODOLOGY-class compute gate ----
# Per Investigating-Workshops.md §"Definition: A WORKSHOP IS": genuine Q1 adversarial adjudication (2 agents,
# competing readings of a substrate-IS structural claim, R1/R2/R3, STRUCTURAL VERDICT output). Dispatched via
# /rclab-workshop, NOT /rclab-coordinate. No allowlist append (not a METHODOLOGY-class gate). The verdict-line
# record is the workshop's closure stamp; the corpus/open-channel landing it licenses is a separate follow-up.
```

## Wave 9 → S93+ Decision Point

W9 is a methodology / audit-infrastructure / cross-cutting wave; its outputs feed BOTH this session and S94+ (the cross-cutting Stage-3 sequencing prereq for the 7 Tier-3 STAGE-3-flip gates is the Wave-0 gate W0-1, relocated from this wave):

- **W9-1 / W9-2 (audit-script validators)**: on PASS, both validators are LIVE at the NEXT plan-freeze (S94 and beyond). W9-1 catches registry line-anchor drift; W9-2 catches plan-vs-corpus section-number drift. If either FAILs, the runtime-rescue burden persists and the validator's coverage is a S94 carry-forward.
- **W9-3 (bridge-map-scheme K=3 MANDATORY)**: on PASS, the orchestrator flips `cross-pillar-bridge-anatomy.md §"Bridge-map-scheme suffix discipline"` SUGGESTION → MANDATORY + the corpus §10 K-counter; on FAIL (scheme-DEPENDENT), the discipline stays K=2 SUGGESTION and the ρ-type bridge scheme-dependence is a S94 study. On INFO (HIT axis-(iii) contested), the corpus row lands as SHARED-ANCHOR-COMPANION and the K=3 flip defers to a HIT-distinctness adjudication.
- **W9-4 (per-pole K=3; OPTIONAL/EVOI-gated)**: if dispatched and PASS, the orchestrator flips the per-pole discipline advisory → MANDATORY; if NOT dispatched, it carries forward to S94+ as a genuine compute (DEFERRED, not FAIL).
- **W9-5 (Layer-Functor F workshop)**: VERDICT-A (reformulate) → the K=2-weak narrower theorem statement + corpus fold-in (mack follow-up landing); VERDICT-B (close) → FALSIFIED-at-K=2 promoted to CLOSED in the open-channels ledger. Either way the follow-up registry/corpus/open-channel edit is a separate S93/S94 mack-sole-writer landing.

**Carry-forward (4-field) for S94+** (genuine future computes, NOT hygiene):
- **CF-S94-W9-A** — if W9-4 is NOT dispatched at S93 (EVOI deprioritized): the per-Bulletin-per-pole K=3 closed-form β at a NEW (projector, bridge, pole) triplet. *Inputs*: `_cm_1995_residue_formula.py`, S92 W8-3 npz, new shell-sum S_i(L). *Gate*: max rel_dev ≤ 5% substrate-derived + HIT distinctness. *Effort*: ~1 we.
- **CF-S94-W9-B** — if W9-5 returns VERDICT-A (reformulate) with a deferred FB-saturation compute (INFO hybrid): the Friedrich-Bär saturation cross-observable σ_β re-evaluation at L ∈ [35,100] to test whether σ_β=1.065 persists or saturates. *Inputs*: §W9-3 CF-W6-4-S91-1 npz, FB-saturation predicate, L∈[35,100] scan infra (shared with CF-S94-W5-3). *Gate*: σ_β convergence at the saturation limit. *Effort*: ~1 we (needs L∈[35,100] scan infra, same as CF-S94-W5-3).
